content:
Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results.

And that also appears to be the message Republicans are sending voters ahead of the midterms.

Seriously.

Pollsters say the data is pointing to a potential “blue wave” that could return the House to Democrats, in part because Donald Trump’s approval ratings are at historic lows.

House Republicans are on track to lose their majority unless the party can come up with a message that convinces voters to let them stay in power.

House Speaker Mike Johnson had a chance to articulate one to voters during an interview on CNBC’s "Squawk Box" on Tuesday. Instead, he did the Democrats a big favor.

"For the next two years, what we’re going to do is exactly what we’ve been doing, which is set the conditions for a strong America," Johnson said.

He elaborated:

Johnson tried to win hearts and minds by promising to stay the course on the policies that have led to war with Iran, higher gas prices and inflation. It’s not exactly a winning pitch.

Indeed, the response to that was about as bad as the response to Vice President JD Vance’s thirsty plea earlier this month for voters to “give us another chance.”
